name: Question 10
problem:
Suppose that $f(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty )$ and its Laplace transform

$$
F(s)=L{f(t)}
$$

exists for $s>a.$ Then $F(s)$ is twice differentiable for all $s>a,$ and we have

$$
{F}^{″}(s)=L{{t}^{2}\cdot f(t)}.
$$

A proof of this statement is given below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ $F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}f(t)\,dt$ exists for $s>a.$  

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${F}^{″}(s)=\frac{{d}^{2}}{d{s}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}f(t)\,dt$  

$\text{L3}:\,$ ${F}^{″}(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂{s}^{2}}({e}^{-st}f(t))\,dt$  

$\text{L4}:\,$ $\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂{s}^{2}}({e}^{-st}f(t))={t}^{2}{e}^{-st}f(t)$  

$\text{L5}:\,$ ${F}^{″}(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{t}^{2}{e}^{-st}f(t)\,dt$  

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${F}^{″}(s)=L{{t}^{2}\cdot f(t)}$  

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ and
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ follows from line $\text{L2}$ and
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines $\text{L3}$ and $\text{L4}$ by
{{field-3}}.

Suppose that f(t) is piecewise continuous on [0,∞) and its Laplace transform
F(s)=L{f(t)} exists for s>a. Then F(s) is twice differentiable for all s>a, and we have
F″(s)=L{t2⋅f(t)}.

A proof of this statement is given below.

L1: F(s)=∫0∞e−stf(t)dt exists for s>a.

L2: F″(s)=d2ds2∫0∞e−stf(t)dt

L3: F″(s)=∫0∞∂2∂s2(e−stf(t))dt

L4: ∂2∂s2(e−stf(t))=t2e−stf(t)

L5: F″(s)=∫0∞t2e−stf(t)dt

L6: F″(s)=L{t2⋅f(t)}

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

Line L2 follows from line L1 and
 
the definition of the Laplace transform
differentiating under the integral sign
the definition of the second derivative with respect to s
integration by parts

integrating by parts with respect to s
the continuity of partial derivatives
